course.title: Mental Wellness and Stress
course.tagline: Manage stress, sleep better and build habits that protect your mind.

days.title: What is stress?
days.goal: Learn what stress is and how it feels in the body.

video.title: 7 Science-Backed Ways to Fix Your Stress (That Actually Work)

steps: Watch the video and write down what stress means in your own words.
List 3 signs of stress: fast heartbeat, tight shoulders, racing thoughts.
Write down one thing that stressed you this week.
Notice how your body felt when you were stressed.
days.task: Write 3 signs of stress you have felt.
days.challenge: Notice one stress sign in your body today.

quiz.q: What is stress?
options: The body's response to pressure or demand
quiz.explain: Stress is how the body answers pressure.

quiz.q: What is a sign of stress?
quiz.explain: A fast heart and tight muscles are stress signs.

quiz.q: Why learn about stress?
options: So you can spot it early and act
quiz.explain: Spotting stress early helps you handle it.

days.title: Breathe to calm down
days.goal: Learn slow breathing that calms stress fast.

video.title: Dr Brian Alman Stress Release Workshop

steps: Breathe in for 4 counts through your nose.
Breathe out for 6 counts through your mouth.
Do this 5 times.
Notice how your body feels after.
days.task: Do 5 slow breaths right now.
days.challenge: Use slow breathing once today when you feel tense.

quiz.q: How should you breathe to calm down?
quiz.explain: A long out-breath calms the body.

quiz.q: Why does slow breathing help?
options: It slows the heart and relaxes muscles
quiz.explain: Slow breathing tells the body it is safe.

quiz.q: How many slow breaths should you do?
quiz.explain: Five slow breaths is enough to feel calmer.

days.title: Name what you feel
days.goal: Learn to name your feelings in simple words.
steps: Learn feeling words: happy, sad, angry, scared, tired, calm.
Write down how you feel right now.
Write down why you feel that way.
Say your feeling out loud to yourself.
days.task: Write how you feel right now and why.
days.challenge: Name your feeling 3 times today.

quiz.q: Why name your feelings?
options: Naming a feeling makes it easier to handle
quiz.explain: Naming feelings gives you power over them.

quiz.q: What is a simple feeling word?
quiz.explain: Simple words describe feelings clearly.

quiz.q: What should you do after naming a feeling?
options: Ask what you need right now
quiz.explain: Asking what you need turns feelings into action.

days.title: Move your body to feel better
days.goal: Learn how gentle movement lifts your mood.
steps: Walk for 10 minutes outside.
Stretch your arms and legs gently.
Dance to one song you like.
Write down how you felt after moving.
days.task: Walk for 10 minutes today.
days.challenge: Dance to one song today.

quiz.q: Why does movement help mood?
options: It releases feel-good chemicals in the brain
quiz.explain: Movement lifts mood and eases stress.

quiz.q: How long should you move to feel better?
quiz.explain: Ten minutes of movement can lift your mood.

quiz.q: What is a good mood-lifting move?
quiz.explain: A walk outside clears the mind.

days.title: Sleep well, feel well
days.goal: Learn how sleep protects your mind.
steps: Sleep 7 to 8 hours tonight.
Go to bed at the same time as last night.
Keep your phone away from your bed.
Write down how you felt after good sleep.
days.task: Sleep 7 to 8 hours tonight.
days.challenge: Keep the same bedtime for 3 nights.

quiz.q: Why does sleep help your mind?
options: Sleep clears the mind and steadies mood
quiz.explain: Good sleep helps you think and feel well.

quiz.q: How much sleep should you aim for?
quiz.explain: Seven to eight hours is the healthy aim.

quiz.q: What should you do before bed?
options: Put your phone away and wind down
quiz.explain: Winding down helps you fall asleep.

days.title: Talk to someone you trust
days.goal: Learn why talking helps and how to start.
steps: Pick one person you trust.
Tell them one thing that is on your mind.
Listen to them too.
Write down how you felt after talking.
days.task: Talk to one person you trust today.
days.challenge: Ask a friend how they are doing today.

quiz.q: Why does talking help?
options: It shares the load and brings new ideas
quiz.explain: Talking lightens the load.

quiz.q: Who should you talk to?
quiz.explain: A trusted person listens without judging.

quiz.q: What should you do when a friend talks?
quiz.explain: Listening shows care.

days.title: PROJECT WEEK 1: Your calm toolkit
days.goal: Put week 1 together: build a toolkit of 5 calm tricks.
steps: Pick 5 tricks: slow breathing, walking, naming feelings, talking, stretching.
Write each trick on a card.
Use one trick today.
Keep the cards where you can see them.
days.task: Write your 5 calm tricks on cards.
days.challenge: Use one trick today.

quiz.q: What is a calm toolkit?
options: A set of tricks you use when stressed
quiz.explain: A toolkit is your personal set of calm tricks.

quiz.q: Why write tricks on cards?
options: So you can find them fast when stressed
quiz.explain: Cards make your tricks easy to reach.

quiz.q: How many tricks should your toolkit have?
quiz.explain: Five tricks give you choices.

project.title: Your calm toolkit
project.brief: Build a toolkit of 5 calm tricks on cards: slow breathing, walking, naming feelings, talking and stretching, and use one trick today.
checks: Each trick is on a card

days.title: Spot your stress triggers
days.goal: Learn what sets off your stress.
steps: A trigger is something that starts stress.
Write down 3 things that stressed you this week.
Circle the one that happens most often.
Write one small change for that trigger.
days.task: Write 3 stress triggers from this week.
days.challenge: Write one small change for your biggest trigger.

quiz.q: What is a stress trigger?
quiz.explain: A trigger is what sets stress off.

quiz.q: Why find your triggers?
options: So you can plan for them
quiz.explain: Knowing triggers helps you prepare.

quiz.q: What is a good change for a trigger?
options: One small step, like preparing the night before
quiz.explain: One small change is doable.

days.title: Take a break the right way
days.goal: Learn how to take short breaks that truly rest you.

video.title: Webinar: Ways to deal with Anxiety

steps: Work for 25 minutes, then rest for 5 minutes.
In the break, stand up, stretch and drink water.
Do not check stressful messages in the break.
Use this pattern 3 times today.
days.task: Use the 25-minute work, 5-minute rest pattern once.
days.challenge: Use it 3 times today.

quiz.q: Why take short breaks?
quiz.explain: Short breaks stop tiredness building up.

quiz.q: What should you do in a break?
quiz.explain: Moving and water refresh the body.

quiz.q: How long should a short break be?
quiz.explain: Five minutes is enough to refresh.

days.title: Write it out: journaling
days.goal: Learn to write your thoughts to clear your mind.
steps: Take a notebook and write for 5 minutes.
Write what happened today and how you felt.
Write one thing you are grateful for.
Do not worry about spelling or neatness.
days.task: Write for 5 minutes tonight.
days.challenge: Write every night this week.

quiz.q: What is journaling?
options: Writing your thoughts to clear your mind
quiz.explain: Journaling puts thoughts on paper so they stop spinning.

quiz.q: Why write what you are grateful for?
options: It trains your mind to notice good things
quiz.explain: Gratitude shifts focus to the good.

quiz.q: How long should you journal?
quiz.explain: Five minutes is enough to clear your mind.

days.title: Say no kindly
days.goal: Learn to say no without guilt.

video.title: What is Stress and Anxiety - NHS Webinar

steps: Practise saying: I cannot do that today, but I can help tomorrow.
Say no to one extra task this week.
Notice how you felt after saying no.
Write down one boundary you want to keep.
days.task: Say no kindly to one extra task this week.
days.challenge: Practise your no sentence out loud 3 times.

quiz.q: Why is saying no hard?
options: We worry about letting people down
quiz.explain: Saying no feels hard because we care.

quiz.q: How should you say no?
options: Kindly and clearly, with a reason
quiz.explain: A kind, clear no keeps respect.

quiz.q: What is a boundary?
options: A limit that protects your time and energy
quiz.explain: A boundary is a healthy limit.

days.title: Eat well for your mind
days.goal: Learn how food affects your mood.

video.title: Strategies for Managing Stress and Anxiety - NHS Webinar

steps: Eat regular meals: do not skip breakfast.
Drink water through the day.
Eat less sugar and less caffeine when stressed.
Write down what you ate and how you felt.
days.task: Eat 3 regular meals today.
days.challenge: Drink 6 glasses of water today.

quiz.q: Why eat regular meals?
quiz.explain: Regular meals keep energy and mood steady.

quiz.q: Why drink water?
options: Even mild thirst can make you feel tired and low
quiz.explain: Water keeps the brain working well.

quiz.q: Why cut sugar when stressed?
options: Sugar gives a quick high then a crash
quiz.explain: Sugar crashes make mood worse.

days.title: Move gently: yoga for stress
days.goal: Use gentle yoga to calm stress.

video.title: What is Low Mood - NHS Webinar

steps: Do a slow forward fold with bent knees.
Rest in child's pose for 2 minutes.
Do 5 slow breaths lying on your back.
Notice how your body feels after.
days.task: Do the gentle yoga routine today.
days.challenge: Do it every evening this week.

quiz.q: Why does gentle yoga calm stress?
options: Slow moves and breathing relax the body
quiz.explain: Slow yoga tells the body it is safe.

quiz.q: What is a good pose when stressed?
quiz.explain: Child's pose is restful and safe.

quiz.q: How should you breathe in yoga?
quiz.explain: A long out-breath calms the body.

days.title: PROJECT WEEK 2: Your daily calm routine
days.goal: Put week 2 together: build a daily routine that protects your mind.

video.title: 7 Science-Backed Ways to Fix Your Stress (That Actually Work)

steps: Morning: 5 slow breaths and a 10-minute walk.
Midday: one short break and water.
Evening: journal for 5 minutes and gentle yoga.
Follow the routine for 3 days.
days.task: Write your daily calm routine.
days.challenge: Follow it for 3 days.

quiz.q: What should a calm routine have?
quiz.explain: Small habits through the day protect your mind.

quiz.q: Why follow it for 3 days?
options: To see if it helps before changing it
quiz.explain: Three days shows if the routine works.

quiz.q: What should you do if a habit does not help?
quiz.explain: Swapping keeps the routine working for you.

project.title: Your daily calm routine
project.brief: Build a daily routine: morning breaths and a walk, a midday break, evening journaling and gentle yoga, and follow it for 3 days.
checks: Swapped one habit that did not help

days.title: Meditation for beginners
days.goal: Learn a simple 5-minute meditation.

video.title: Dr Brian Alman Stress Release Workshop

steps: Sit tall with eyes closed or softly open.
Breathe slowly and count each out-breath to 10, then start again.
When your mind wanders, bring it back kindly.
Sit for 5 minutes.
days.task: Meditate for 5 minutes today.
days.challenge: Meditate every morning this week.

quiz.q: What is meditation?
options: Sitting quietly and noticing your breath
quiz.explain: Meditation is quiet time with your breath.

quiz.q: What should you do when your mind wanders?
quiz.explain: Wandering is normal; bring the mind back gently.

quiz.q: How long should a beginner meditate?
quiz.explain: Five minutes is a good start.

days.title: Handle worry with a plan
days.goal: Learn to turn worry into a small plan.
steps: Write down what you are worried about.
Ask: what can I do about it today?
Write one small step and do it.
Set a worry time: 10 minutes, then stop.
days.task: Write one worry and one small step today.
days.challenge: Use a 10-minute worry time today.

quiz.q: Why write worries down?
options: It stops them spinning in your head
quiz.explain: Writing worries down makes them smaller.

quiz.q: What is a worry time?
options: A set 10 minutes to worry, then stop
quiz.explain: A set worry time contains the worry.

quiz.q: What should you do after worry time?
options: Do one small step or let it go
quiz.explain: A small step turns worry into action.

days.title: Digital breaks: rest your mind
days.goal: Learn to take breaks from screens.
steps: Put your phone away for 1 hour today.
Turn off notifications for one evening.
Do something offline: walk, read, cook.
Write down how you felt after the break.
days.task: Put your phone away for 1 hour today.
days.challenge: Have one screen-free evening this week.

quiz.q: Why take breaks from screens?
options: Screens can feed stress and steal sleep
quiz.explain: Screen breaks rest the mind.

quiz.q: What should you do instead of screens?
quiz.explain: Offline activities refresh the mind.

quiz.q: How long should a screen break be?
quiz.explain: One hour is a good start.

days.title: Be kind to yourself
days.goal: Learn self-compassion: talk to yourself like a friend.
steps: Notice one harsh thought you had today.
Rewrite it kindly: I am learning, and that is OK.
Say one kind thing to yourself each morning.
Write down 3 things you did well this week.
days.task: Say one kind thing to yourself today.
days.challenge: Write 3 things you did well this week.

quiz.q: What is self-compassion?
options: Talking to yourself kindly, like a friend
quiz.explain: Self-compassion is kind self-talk.

quiz.q: Why rewrite harsh thoughts?
options: Kind words help you keep going
quiz.explain: Kind self-talk builds strength.

quiz.q: What should you do when you make a mistake?
options: Learn from it and move on
quiz.explain: Mistakes are how we learn.

days.title: Build good habits, one at a time
days.goal: Learn how habits form and how to build one.
steps: Pick one small habit: a 5-minute walk after lunch.
Do it at the same time every day.
Tick it off on a calendar each day.
After 2 weeks, add one more habit.
days.task: Pick one small habit and do it today.
days.challenge: Tick it off on your calendar.

quiz.q: How do habits form?
options: By doing a small thing at the same time each day
quiz.explain: Repeating a small thing builds a habit.

quiz.q: Why start with one habit?
options: One habit is doable; many at once fail
quiz.explain: One habit at a time sticks.

quiz.q: Why tick habits off?
quiz.explain: Ticks show your streak.

days.title: Help a friend who is stressed
days.goal: Learn how to support a stressed friend.
steps: Listen without judging or fixing.
Ask: what would help right now?
Offer one small thing: a walk, a talk, a meal.
Check in again tomorrow.
days.task: Ask a friend how they are doing today.
days.challenge: Offer one small help to a friend.

quiz.q: What is the best first step?
quiz.explain: Listening shows care.

quiz.q: What should you ask a stressed friend?
quiz.explain: Asking what helps respects their needs.

quiz.q: Why check in again tomorrow?
quiz.explain: Checking in again shows real care.

days.title: PROJECT WEEK 3: Your wellness plan
days.goal: Put week 3 together: write your own 7-day wellness plan.
steps: Pick one habit for morning, midday and evening.
Add one walk and one talk with a friend each day.
Add one screen-free hour each evening.
Follow the plan for 7 days.
days.task: Write your 7-day wellness plan.
days.challenge: Follow it for 7 days.

quiz.q: What should a wellness plan have?
quiz.explain: Small habits through the day protect your mind.

quiz.q: Why follow it for 7 days?
options: A week shows if the plan works
quiz.explain: A week of practice shows real change.

quiz.q: What should you do if a day goes badly?
quiz.explain: One bad day does not ruin the plan.

project.title: Your wellness plan
project.brief: Write your own 7-day wellness plan with morning, midday and evening habits, a daily walk, a daily talk and a screen-free hour, and follow it for 7 days.
checks: Plan has morning, midday and evening habits

days.title: Know when to ask for help
days.goal: Learn the signs that mean you should talk to a doctor or counsellor.

video.title: Webinar: Ways to deal with Anxiety

steps: Signs: feeling low for more than 2 weeks, cannot sleep, cannot eat.
Asking for help is strong, not weak.
Write down who you would call: a doctor, a helpline, a trusted person.
Keep the number where you can find it.
days.task: Write down who you would call for help.
days.challenge: Keep the number in your phone.

quiz.q: When should you ask for professional help?
options: When low feelings last more than 2 weeks
quiz.explain: Long-lasting low feelings need expert help.

quiz.q: Is asking for help weak?
options: No, it is strong and smart
quiz.explain: Asking for help takes courage.

quiz.q: Who can you ask for help?
options: A doctor, a counsellor or a helpline
quiz.explain: Doctors and counsellors are trained to help.

days.title: Gratitude: notice the good
days.goal: Learn a simple gratitude habit.
steps: Each night, write 3 good things from the day.
They can be small: a good meal, a kind word, sunshine.
Say thank you to one person each week.
Do this for 7 nights.
days.task: Write 3 good things tonight.
days.challenge: Say thank you to one person this week.

quiz.q: What is gratitude?
quiz.explain: Gratitude is noticing the good.

quiz.q: Why write 3 good things each night?
options: It trains your mind to notice the good
quiz.explain: Noticing good things lifts mood.

quiz.q: How small can a good thing be?
options: As small as a kind word or sunshine
quiz.explain: Small good things count just as much.

days.title: Review your month
days.goal: Look back at your month of wellness work.

video.title: What is Stress and Anxiety - NHS Webinar

steps: Read your notes from weeks 1 to 3.
List 3 tricks that helped you most.
List 1 thing that is still hard.
Write one fix for the hard thing.
days.task: List 3 tricks that helped you most.
days.challenge: Fix one hard thing in your routine.

quiz.q: Why review your month?
options: To see what helped and what needs fixing
quiz.explain: Reviewing shows real progress.

quiz.q: What should you do with a hard thing?
options: Fix it with one small change
quiz.explain: One small fix keeps the plan going.

quiz.q: What is a sign your toolkit works?
quiz.explain: Feeling calmer more often means it works.

days.title: Teach a friend your calm tricks
days.goal: Teach someone else what helped you.

video.title: Strategies for Managing Stress and Anxiety - NHS Webinar

steps: Show a friend your calm toolkit cards.
Teach them slow breathing.
Walk together for 10 minutes.
Ask them how they felt after.
days.task: Teach slow breathing to one person.
days.challenge: Walk with a friend this week.

quiz.q: Why teach someone else?
options: Teaching helps you learn it better
quiz.explain: Teaching locks in your own learning.

quiz.q: What is the first trick to teach?
quiz.explain: Slow breathing is simple and works fast.

quiz.q: Why walk together?
options: Walking and talking help both of you
quiz.explain: A shared walk helps two people at once.

days.title: Build a calm morning routine
days.goal: Learn a calm morning routine.

video.title: What is Low Mood - NHS Webinar

steps: Wake up at the same time each day.
Drink water and stretch for 5 minutes.
Write down 1 thing you want to do today.
Eat a simple breakfast.
Avoid your phone for the first 15 minutes.
Leave the house on time, not in a rush.
days.task: Try the calm morning routine tomorrow.
days.challenge: Do the routine for 3 mornings in a row.

quiz.q: Why avoid your phone first thing?
options: It fills your mind with noise before the day starts
quiz.explain: A quiet start keeps your mind calm.

quiz.q: What should you write down in the morning?
options: One thing you want to do today
quiz.explain: One clear goal gives the day direction.

quiz.q: Why wake up at the same time?
options: It helps your body clock stay steady
quiz.explain: A steady wake time helps you sleep better too.

days.title: Handle a hard day
days.goal: Learn what to do when a day goes badly.

video.title: 7 Science-Backed Ways to Fix Your Stress (That Actually Work)

steps: Stop and take 5 slow breaths.
Name what went wrong in one sentence.
Pick one small thing you can fix.
Talk to someone you trust.
Do one kind thing for yourself.
Write down what you learned.
days.task: Write down your plan for a hard day.
days.challenge: Use the plan the next time a day goes badly.

quiz.q: What is the first step on a hard day?
quiz.explain: Slow breaths calm you before you act.

quiz.q: Why name what went wrong?
options: So it feels smaller and clearer
quiz.explain: Naming a problem makes it easier to fix.

quiz.q: Why do one kind thing for yourself?
options: It helps you feel better and keep going
quiz.explain: Kindness to yourself builds strength.

days.title: Get ready for your capstone
days.goal: Review the whole course and prepare your final project.

video.title: Dr Brian Alman Stress Release Workshop

steps: Read your notes from weeks 1 to 4.
List 5 tricks you can now use when stressed.
Practise your capstone routine once.
Write down any questions you still have.
days.task: List 5 calm tricks you learned.
days.challenge: Do your capstone routine from memory.

quiz.q: What is the capstone?
options: A final project that shows what you learned
quiz.explain: The capstone is your final show of skill.

quiz.q: What should you review before the capstone?
options: Your notes from all four weeks
quiz.explain: Reviewing all weeks brings the course together.

quiz.q: How do you know you are ready?
options: You can use your toolkit calmly when stressed
quiz.explain: Using your tricks calmly shows you are ready.

days.title: Final practice day
days.goal: Practise your capstone once more, then rest.
steps: Do your capstone routine one more time.
Check your toolkit cards are ready.
Fix anything that felt rushed.
Rest well tonight.
days.task: Run your capstone routine and time each part.
days.challenge: Fix one thing that felt rushed.

quiz.q: Why practise once more?
options: Practice makes the real run calm and smooth
quiz.explain: Practice turns worry into calm confidence.

quiz.q: What should you check after practice?
options: Your tricks, your timing and your breathing
quiz.explain: Checking your tricks makes the routine smooth.

quiz.q: What should you do the night before?
quiz.explain: Good rest helps you do your best.

days.title: Capstone day: your wellness plan
days.goal: Show what you learned: present your wellness plan and use your toolkit.
steps: Show your 7-day wellness plan.
Teach slow breathing to one person.
Do your calm routine from start to finish.
Write a short report on your month.
days.task: Present your plan, teach breathing and write your report.
days.challenge: Hand in your report and celebrate.

quiz.q: What should your plan show?
options: 7 days of habits that protect your mind
quiz.explain: A full plan shows real skill.

quiz.q: What is the first trick to teach?
quiz.explain: Slow breathing is simple and works fast.

quiz.q: What goes in your report?
options: What you did and what you learned
quiz.explain: A short report shows what you learned.

capstone.title: Your wellness plan
capstone.brief: Present your 7-day wellness plan, teach slow breathing to one person, do your calm routine from start to finish, and write a short report on your month.
checks: Kept a journal for a week
deliverables: A short video or notes from teaching
